instructions.description: Deposit tokens from the rebalancer into the pool's token account, backing release on inbound transfers.

flags.description: Lockrelease token pool program ID (required for all instructions)
Token mint address (required for all instructions)
Authority address (required for all instructions)
Amount to provide/withdraw (in smallest token units) (required for provide/withdraw-liquidity)
provide-liquidity only: prepend the SPL Approve for the pool signer PDA, so the delegation cannot be spent or replaced before the transfer

instructions.preconditions: Three gates, in order: a rebalancer must be set, can-accept-liquidity must be true, and the rebalancer's token account must have approved the POOL SIGNER PDA as delegate (the program moves tokens by CPI with that PDA as authority). That approval is NOT one-time setup: the transfer spends it and SPL clears the delegate at zero, and a ccipSend approves the router's fee-billing signer on the same account, replacing it. Approve immediately before each provide-liquidity, or pass --auto-approve to put both in one transaction.
instructions.failure_modes: Missing rebalancer -> Unauthorized 6002. Liquidity disabled -> LiquidityNotAccepted 6020. Missing, spent or replaced delegate approval -> SPL Token OwnerMismatch (custom program error 0x4) raised inside the CPI, naming neither the delegate nor the amount; the CLI checks the delegation first and prints the account state instead.

instructions.when_to_use: Verify a deployment, or hand one over. One command covers the roles that are easy to forget: who can still extend the lookup table the router reads on every send, whether the pool token account carries a delegate, and whether the mint has Token-2022 extensions that change what a transfer does. It does not report the pool program's upgrade authority.

instructions.description: Create an SPL mint under a seed-derived address, optionally with metadata and an initial supply minted to a recipient.

flags.description: Payer/authority public key
Recipient address (for mint instruction or create-mint initial supply)
Token decimals (0-255, required for create-mint)
Token program: spl-token or token-2022 (default: spl-token)
Create with Metaplex metadata (true/false)
Metadata backend for create-mint: none, metaplex (separate PDA, any token program) or token-2022 (embedded in the mint, requires --token-program token-2022). Overrides --with-metaplex
Token name (required if with-metaplex=true, max 32 chars)
Token symbol (required if with-metaplex=true, max 10 chars)
Metadata URI (required if with-metaplex=true)
Initial supply in smallest units (optional)

instructions.preconditions: Pick the metadata backend with --metadata: 'metaplex' writes a separate Metaplex PDA (either token program), 'token-2022' embeds it in the mint via the TokenMetadata extension and requires --token-program token-2022. --with-metaplex true is an alias for 'metaplex'. The embedded backend is creation-only: Token-2022 extensions are initialized before InitializeMint, so an existing mint can never gain the TokenMetadata extension, whereas Metaplex metadata can be attached later.
instructions.failure_modes: The backend decides which instruction can later change the metadata authority; see docs/gotchas #metadata-backend-decides-the-instruction. Freeze authority is set to the mint authority. The mint address is random per run (auto-generated seed).

instructions.preconditions: --mint is required to detect the correct token program and --seed to derive the account address.
instructions.failure_modes: SPL multisigs are IMMUTABLE: members and threshold cannot be changed afterwards. The token program never checks threshold <= signers, so such a multisig would initialize and be permanently unusable; this CLI refuses it. Max 11 signers. See docs/gotchas #mint-authority-multisig.
